correctness.rationale: The closed neighborhoods of the complement omit exactly the two cycle neighbors. For n>=5 these omitted pairs are the distinct edges of a two-regular auxiliary graph, one n-cycle for odd n or two n/2-cycles for even n. Equal selected-edge intersections arise exactly from two empty edges or from an isolated selected vertex; pairwise distinct traces force |S|>=3 and hence nonempty identification. A valid component word has no 010 and globally at most one 00. The complete cyclic stars-and-bars counts A_m and B_m, including the unique marked double-zero run, prove the full polynomial for every n>=5. The generating functions yield N_n=(1+cn)lambda^n+O(n*1.2^n) from the unique dominant simple root. The extracted SymPy checker proves an independent exact 16-state determinant identity and verifies all 2^n subsets for n=5..16 against both enumerators; the infinite claim rests on the written proof, not extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The 2020 source addresses minimum identifying-code cardinalities of complements of cycles. The accessible 2006 full text treats radius-r identifying-code minima on cycles, including equivalent odd-cycle excluded-pair geometry. The 2026 OLD cycle census actually covers the A zero-defect term and is fully credited. It does not count code configurations with exactly one unoccupied auxiliary edge, the B term that contributes a linearly growing multiplicative factor and is the new all-sizes result. Full text of the 2020 source could not be obtained; this is explicitly retained as a meaningful residual priority risk. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches found no full all-size complement-cycle enumeration.
residual_risks: The exact 2020 complement-cycle minimum-code publication is highly relevant but its eight-page full text could not be read; a previously stated full polynomial cannot be conclusively excluded.
Unindexed, differently named, or later counting literature may contain an equivalent binomial correction.
The result has undergone only same-model mathematical review, not independent external validation.

value.rationale: The complement of a cycle is a canonical dense graph family with a previously published identifying-code minimum but not a verified complete size census. The exact correction B counts all single-defect configurations, often changes the minimum layer, and dominates the zero-defect OLD family by a factor asymptotic to cn. The theorem provides all cardinalities, parity-sensitive products, a sharp cyclic structural characterization, and a common-parity leading growth law; this is a motivated complete classification, not a routine isolated table lookup.
